issues.title: MY2004–05 Saab 9-5 B235 manual oil-trap campaign is not all-years PCV fitment

vin_ranges.kind: factory stated range; selected cars only

issues.cause: Factory CSP15433 was selective, limited by VIN/engine/gearbox and engine-number subcase; cross-referenced retailer parts may be listed more broadly.
symptoms: seller says universal upgraded oil trap
oil consumption at light load and high rpm
issues.diagnosis_summary: Check exact VIN against Saab CSP15433 records and completion, transmission and engine stamping, inspect actual hose retention and seal condition; keep 15435 separate.
issues.correction_summary: Follow verified campaign/workshop documents for included vehicles, otherwise verify original EPC part before a later model repair.
limits: VIN range alone does not prove inclusion.
Campaign part number not globally fit for MY2006–09.
No confirmed reliability upgrade or bearing-condition result.

issues.title: 9-5 radiator choice must distinguish automatic cooler fittings
issues.cause: Factory WIS describes oil-cooler lines on automatic radiator; parts retailer separately lists distinct manual and automatic radiator references.
symptoms: radiator replacement quote assumes one universal 9-5 B235 radiator
automatic fluid leaks at cooler unions
issues.diagnosis_summary: Identify installed automatic vs manual gearbox, radiator cooler ports and lines, radiator mounting and hose end geometry; perform cold-system pressure test as applicable.
issues.correction_summary: Select correct VIN/gearbox-certified component and follow WIS coolant/automatic fluid leak and level checks.
limits: Vendor reference is not official OEM supersession.
Use no automatic radiator 'upgrade' without manufacturer approval.
Do not extend 9-3 FA57 coolant/ATF bulletin to original 9-5 as proof of same failure.

issues.title: Left mount and front torque arm fastener values change at chassis 73514478/73514479
issues.cause: Saab WIS provides distinct central nut and mounting bracket torque based on exact vehicle-identifier boundary.
symptoms: mount replacement uses generic torque chart
used gearbox mount or bracket history unknown
engine mount preload and vibration after repair
issues.diagnosis_summary: Confirm stamped VIN suffix, manual/automatic gearbox and exact bolt location; inspect mount alignment and correct fastener version.
issues.correction_summary: Use factory procedure and vehicle-bound torque path; replacement component choice still requires OEM WebEPC fitment.
limits: Change in torque is NOT evidence that specific part numbers superseded.
VIN suffix boundary not mapped to particular MY production date.
Procedural torques not an instruction to work beneath unsupported engine.
